sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial skeleton that includes a skull but is not articulated. The bones are largely three-dimensionally preserved with little compression and belong to a subadult individual.

Because the name was published electronically, Life Science Identifiers were required to validate the taxon's name. This discovery represents the first direct evidence of sympatry among pterosaurs, showing direct association rather than just co-occurrence in the same stratigraphic unit.
The species Keresdrakon vilsoni was named and described in 2019 by Kellner, Weinschütz, Holgado, Bantim, and Sayão.

Fossils of Keresdrakon were found in direct association with Caiuajara and Vespersaurus, confirming these species were sympatric. In the bone beds, Keresdrakon was the least common of the three pterosaur taxa present, while Caiuajara was the most common.
Researchers suggest that Keresdrakon may have been an opportunistic predator in its desert environment, based on its azhdarchid-like rostrum.

Keresdrakon lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian to Albian stages, between 125 and 100.5 million years ago. Sedimentological data indicates that the environment of the Goio-Erê Formation was a desert.

The age of the Goio-Erê Formation is disputed, ranging potentially from the Aptian to the Campanian. The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Keresdrakon as Aptian to Campanian, from 121.4 to 72.2 million years ago.
